title: Systems, Work and Mechanical Advantage
seo_title: Grade 8 Science: Systems, Work and Mechanical Advantage Worksheets (Ontario Curriculum)
standard_text: Describe systems in terms of inputs, outputs, components and subsystems; calculate work, mechanical advantage and efficiency; explain how friction and design affect a system's efficiency. (summary of the Ontario Science and Technology curriculum, 2022, Strand D: Structures and Mechanisms – Systems in Action)
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 science worksheets on systems, inputs and outputs, work, mechanical advantage, efficiency and simple machines. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Work = force × distance; MA = load ÷ effort; efficiency = output ÷ input × 100%.
body_html:
How to think about it

A system is a set of parts working together. It has inputs, outputs and often subsystems.

  • Work = force × distance, measured in joules (J).
  • Mechanical advantage = load ÷ effort. A ramp, lever or pulley can give MA greater than 1.
  • Efficiency = useful work out ÷ work in × 100%. Friction lowers efficiency.
Example

A lever lifts 300 N with 50 N of effort. What is the MA?

300 ÷ 50

Answer: 6

Example

A motor uses 500 J and does 400 J of useful work. Efficiency?

400 ÷ 500 × 100%

Answer: 80%

Common mistakes

  • Thinking machines reduce the work needed (they reduce the force, not the work).
  • Thinking a machine can be more than 100% efficient.
  • Calling it work when nothing moves.

items.q: Which is an example of a social system?
items.e: Social systems are groups of people and things working together.

items.q: What is feedback in a system?
c: information from the output that is used to adjust the system
items.e: A thermostat uses feedback.

items.q: What kind of mechanism is used in a crowbar?
items.e: Levers, pulleys and gears are simple machines.

items.q: Which shows the main energy conversion in an electric kettle?
c: chemical potential energy → electrical energy → light energy and thermal energy
kinetic energy of the wind → electrical energy
items.e: The useful output depends on the job of an electric kettle.

items.q: How can the efficiency of a bike be improved?
c: oil the chain and pump up the tires
items.e: Less friction, more useful output.

items.q: Which shows the main energy conversion in a catapult firing a stone?

items.e: The useful output depends on the job of a catapult firing a stone.

items.q: Which simple machine is a screw?
items.e: A screw is an inclined plane wrapped around a cylinder.

items.q: What kind of mechanism is used in a mechanical clock?
items.e: Levers, pulleys and gears are simple machines.

items.q: What kind of mechanism is used in a bottle opener?
items.e: Levers, pulleys and gears are simple machines.

items.q: How has automation changed factories?
c: It made products slower to make.
Robots do repetitive jobs, raising output but changing the jobs people do.
items.e: Systems affect society.

items.q: Which shows the main energy conversion in a person running?
c: kinetic energy of the wind → electrical energy
chemical potential energy → kinetic energy and thermal energy
items.e: The useful output depends on the job of a person running.

items.q: Why can no machine be 100% efficient?
c: Some energy is always lost, mostly as heat from friction.
items.e: Lubrication reduces friction.

items.q: Which is an environmental cost of a transportation system?

items.e: Public transit can reduce the cost.

items.q: Which simple machine is a wedge?
items.e: A wedge splits things apart.

items.q: What kind of mechanism is used in tweezers?
items.e: Levers, pulleys and gears are simple machines.

items.q: Which shows the main energy conversion in a bow shooting an arrow?
c: kinetic energy → thermal energy and sound energy
chemical potential energy → thermal energy and light energy
elastic potential energy → kinetic energy of the arrow
items.e: The useful output depends on the job of a bow shooting an arrow.

items.q: What is the output of a system?
items.e: Forward motion is the output of a bike.

items.q: In science, when is work done?
c: when you push a wall that does not move
when a force moves an object through a distance
items.e: Work = force × distance.

items.q: What happens to the output of a system if one subsystem fails?
c: The whole system may stop working or work poorly.
items.e: Subsystems depend on each other.

items.q: Why do ramps make it easier to move a wheelchair up a step?
c: A longer slope means less force is needed (but over a longer distance).
items.e: Inclined planes trade distance for force.

items.q: A student pushes a box with a force of 50 N for 5 m. How much work is done?
items.e: Work = force × distance = 50 N × 5 m = 250 J.

items.q: What is a system?
c: a group of parts that work together to do a job
items.e: A bicycle is a mechanical system.

items.q: A light bulb receives 200 J of electrical energy and gives out 40 J of light energy. How much energy is converted to thermal energy?
items.e: Total energy out = total energy in: 200 − 40 = 160 J.

items.q: Noah lifts a bag with a force of 40 N for 0.5 m. How much work is done?
items.e: work done = force × distance = 40 × 0.5 = 20 J.

items.q: Why might a city choose a light rail system?
c: It moves many people with less traffic and pollution.
items.e: Systems are judged by many criteria.

items.q: A ball dropped with 60 J of potential energy bounces back up with 45 J. Where did the rest of the energy go?
